analysis:
Examined both documentation changes, metadata, patches and supplied surrounding text against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. Installation.md head lines 219–255 adds operator-initiated predecessor rollback, confirmation, request draining, journaled replacement, quarantine and cluster-stop guidance; troubleshooting.md head lines 151–152 documents the same quarantine behavior. No executable control changes or independently supported security regression appear in this scope. Existing installer verification, coordinator binding, attestation guidance, fan-helper separation and diagnostic/report exposure descriptions are unchanged; unrelated pre-existing documentation issues are not findings.
Integration must verify the new documented behavior in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Update/UpdateInstallLayout.swift (snapshotLiveAsPredecessor), UpdateRecoveryState.swift and darkbloom/UpdateCommand.swift: validate retained signed artifacts before execution, serialize rollback with updates/watchdog recovery, drain without reopening admission prematurely, refuse active cluster rollback, and preserve crash-safe swap/restart behavior. Relevant contracts are T-043/T-013 (replaceable recovery authority), T-053/T-054/T-052 (rollback must not preserve stale grants or imply qualification), T-047 (root helper lifecycle) and T-041 (older code/cache compatibility must retain confidentiality and scope bindings). These implementations are not supplied, so their controls cannot be judged here. No evidence establishes an older vulnerable deployment or an authorization bypass from the documentation alone. Deeper integration review is needed for the rollback implementation and its current-build authorization interactions, not for unchanged dependencies generally.
